Good morning, Elena. Your reservation at Maison Verre is confirmed for the seventeenth. I've added the citrus orchard view you mentioned last June — the same room as before. Anything else I should prepare?

Thank you, that's wonderful. One question — our flight lands at Nice at 22:40, so we'll likely reach the house close to midnight. Will the side gate code still work at that hour, or should I ring you?
13:51 · from Elena
— Wednesday, 15 May —
Not to worry, the gate code is active around the clock. I'll leave the courtyard lantern on and a light supper — olives, bread, the local rosé — on the marble counter. Drive safely.
08:24 · me
A late check-in on Friday — is the side gate still the easiest entrance, or should we ring the main door? Also: could we possibly add a bottle of the Bandol you served last time? We'd happily pay for it directly.
10:08 · from Elena
Of course — the Bandol will be waiting, alongside two glasses. The side gate is best at that hour; the main door will hold its lights to echo into the neighbouring courtyard. Travel well.

INTERNAL NOTES

"Elena was thrilled with the orchard view in June — she lingered there each morning with a book. Worth recreating."

— Camille, 14 May 2025

On the first reply, a guest's enquiry is a doorway. Answer within the hour, in the voice you'd use at the threshold itself.

On the small ask. A bottle of Bandol, a later check-in, a pillow firmer than the last. Note it, do it, never ask twice.

On the silence afterward. Not every message wants a reply. A read receipt and a lit lantern, at midnight, will speak for themselves.
